body:
> Problem: when the user selects a specific facet value I want to hide the refinement list

This does not feel like a real world example. The need of hiding the pagination is real. Even if it was only requested by us internally, we never waited for users to tell us something was broken to fix it if we spotted it.

The CSS classes we added to our widgets already helped us a lot in adding UI features. I really don't see how this is different from the `active` classes we add to our refinement list. We could have stayed with a checkbox that is ticked or not, but adding a wrapping CSS class let users do much more than this. CSS classes are the only way currently that users can interact with the internal state of the components.

I think that the problem is more generic than this issue only. We need to have a way for users to change the display based on the widget/component state. Either we expose it through `render` events, or through CSS classes or any other methods is up to us. But I feel like whatever the method we chose, we will still increase the API surface for any new part of the state we expose, and have to document it.

And as we already started exposing state through CSS in this v1, we should keep doing it and think about a better way for a v2.
